snap.why: The protests provide evidence of citizen participation, political power, authority and social change.
Ummah can reinforce collective Muslim identity and a sense of belonging.
Content analysis systematically examines material to identify patterns, themes or trends.
Westernisation is a process of social and cultural influence, not a research method.
Salah is the Islamic practice of prayer and can reinforce identity and continuity.
Streaming technologies influence access to and consumption of film.
Micro refers primarily to individuals and close interpersonal relationships; national institutions operate at a broader level.
Focus groups commonly collect qualitative data through guided group discussion.
Modernisation and Westernisation can overlap but are not the same process.
Concentrated media ownership provides evidence for examining power and control in popular culture.

truefalse.q: Modernisation and Westernisation mean exactly the same thing.
truefalse.why: They may interact, but modernisation does not necessarily require adopting Western culture.

truefalse.q: Micro, meso and macro help examine society at different levels.
truefalse.why: They allow analysis from individuals and close relationships through groups/institutions to wider society.

truefalse.q: A focus group normally involves a moderator guiding discussion.
truefalse.why: The moderator helps structure discussion among participants.

truefalse.q: Ummah can be used as evidence for identity and belonging in Islam.
truefalse.why: It refers to the wider Muslim community and supports collective belonging.

truefalse.q: An example automatically becomes analysis simply because it is specific.
truefalse.why: The response must explain what the example demonstrates and connect it to the question.

truefalse.q: Streaming technologies can influence access to and consumption of Teen Film.
truefalse.why: Distribution technologies affect how and where audiences access film.

truefalse.q: The Candlelight Revolution is useful only as an example of technology.
truefalse.why: It is especially useful for power, authority, citizenship, participation, continuity and change.

truefalse.q: Content analysis can be used to investigate trends in popular culture.
truefalse.why: Researchers can code and compare recurring content, representations or themes.

truefalse.q: A 15-mark Evaluate response should avoid making a judgement until the conclusion.
truefalse.why: A judgement should be established and sustained throughout the response.

truefalse.q: Salah, Ramadan, Hajj and Zakat can provide evidence for continuity in Islam.
truefalse.why: Rituals and practices help transmit and maintain beliefs and identity over time.

truefalse.q: Globalisation can produce both continuity and change.
truefalse.why: Global influences can create change while local cultures adapt them and retain existing traditions.

truefalse.q: Teen Film should be studied only as a collection of film plots.
truefalse.why: The depth study examines development, consumption, access, control, identity, technology, globalisation and change.

wheel.q: Name one example that could demonstrate power or authority.
wheel.a: The 2016–17 Candlelight Revolution is one strong example.

wheel.q: What is the difference between modernisation and Westernisation?
wheel.a: Modernisation concerns broader social/economic/technological development; Westernisation specifically concerns Western cultural influence.

wheel.q: Name one technology that has changed access to Teen Film.
wheel.a: Streaming services are a strong example because they alter distribution and audience access.

wheel.q: Name one class film that could be used as evidence.
wheel.a: 10 Things I Hate About You or Do Revenge.

wheel.q: Give one example of a ritual that can reinforce continuity.
wheel.a: Examples include Salah, Ramadan, Hajj or Zakat.
